result.topic_en: Latin draft (page 10) of Riemann's Paris prize essay on heat conduction, treating the reduction of the heat equation $\Delta u = \partial u/\partial t$ to linear equations among functions, and the case $n=2$ where the solution has the form $ap+bq+c$.
result.transcription:
10.
expressio in aequatione
$\Delta u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
substituitur, obtinetur aequatio formae
$\Sigma PQ = 0$
in qua quantitates $Q$ sunt quotientes differen-
tiales ipsarum $q$ ideoque functiones solarum
$\beta$ et $t$, quantitates $P$ autem functiones solarum
$\alpha$ et $\beta$. At tali aequationi supra vidimus, si
ex $n$ terminis componatur, subjacere $\mu$ aequa-
tiones lineares inter functiones $Q$ et $n-\mu$
aequationes inter functiones $P$, quarum coeffi-
cientes sunt functiones solius $\beta$, denotante
$\mu$ quempiam numerorum $0, 1, 2, \ldots n$. Obtine-
buntur igitur expressiones ipsarum $\frac{\partial q}{\partial t}$ per
quotientes differentiales ipsarum $q$ secundum
$\beta$ ab ipsa $\alpha$ liberae. -
Jam casus singulos problematis nostri ad
hunc casum pertinentes perlustremus.
Quando $m = 2$ et $\Delta$ est formae $\partial_\alpha \partial_\beta + e\,\partial_\alpha + f\,\partial_\beta$
aequatio reducta $\Delta\, \Delta u = 0$, si a quotientibus
differentialibus secundum $\beta$ libera evadit, formam
induet:
$\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial \alpha^3} + r\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial \alpha^2} + s\frac{\partial u}{\partial \alpha} = 0$
unde $u$ erit formae
$ap + bq + c$
denotantibus $a, b, c$ functiones solarum $\beta$ et $t$
$p$ et $q$ autem functiones solarum $\alpha$ et $\beta$. Jam
in locum ipsius $\alpha$ variabilis independens $q$ in-
troduci [-pot-] potest. Quo pacto obtinetur
$u = ap + \alpha b + c$
ubi jam sola $p$ est functio ambarum varia-
bilium $\alpha$ et $\beta$. Substituendo hanc expressionem
in aequationibus
$\Delta u = 0 \quad \Delta u = \frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$
coëfficientium formae facile eruuntur.
Restat casus quando jam una aequationum,
in quas aequatio $F = 0$ discinditur[?], formam (1,
habet, ideoque formam

methods.what: Substituting the ansatz into the heat equation yields a bilinear relation sum P Q = 0 with P depending on (alpha, beta) and Q on (beta, t)
A bilinear relation of n terms splits into mu linear relations among the Q and n-mu among the P, with coefficients depending only on beta

methods.what: Case m=2: the reduced equation becomes a third-order linear ODE in alpha
General form of the solution of this ODE
Change of independent variable from alpha to q, giving a simplified form of u

items.english: Let us now examine the individual cases of our problem that pertain to this case.

in aequationibus

coëfficientium formae facile eruuntur.
items.english: By substituting this expression into the equations Δu = 0 and Δu = ∂u/∂t, the forms of the coefficients are easily found.
